alignments.note: Retain gam etmol gam shilshom as one noncompositional rendering of In times past: etmol and shilshom jointly name the former period, and the first gam opens the correlation whose second gam includes the further temporal member; their cumulative force is read within the plural times past. No separate English allocation to either noun or particle is non-arbitrary. A competing reading leaves each gam unrepresented as additive emphasis and gives the English idiom to etmol + shilshom; that remains defensible, but is not clearly preferable to the correlative reading here (rules 2, 8, 30). No English word writes either noun's own lexeme, so s001 remains the first-token fallback source head (rule 6), with past as target head.

variant_decisions.evidence: ASV 'it was thou that leddest out' renders a 2ms 'thou wast'; the ketiv הייתה is a plene spelling of the same 2ms form and the English shows nothing that separates the two spellings. The only note is alternative_rendering ('Or, leader') on a different word. Base qere fallback carries the projection.

Qere הַמּוֹצִיא has the article, ketiv מוציא lacks it; ASV 'that leddest out' is a relative participle rendering that either an articular or anarthrous participle yields. No note maps to this unit. Base qere fallback carries the projection.

Ketiv והמבי differs from qere וְהַמֵּבִיא only by the dropped final aleph, an orthographic variant of the same hiphil participle; ASV 'and broughtest in' cannot distinguish spellings. No note maps to this unit. Base qere fallback carries the projection.

alignments.note: Halokh contributes ongoing progression and gadol supplies greatness; the repeated comparative greater ... greater jointly renders those contributions. Assigning the first greater independently to halokh would give that infinitive a lexical meaning it does not carry. Rule 56's distinct-adverb condition is unmet, so rule 2 retains the joint rendering, headed on gadol and the first greater. The finite halak retains waxed and the waw retains and.

review_notes: Corrected: 'to' before Gezer moved from the infinitive bo' to the place name. Gezer is an adverbial accusative of direction, not the verb's direct object, so rule 33 governs the supplied preposition and rule 44's supplied-object clause does not reach it; this matches the chapter's treatment of 'to Jerusalem' at 2SA.5.6.
